results.title: HS Code for Printed Circuit Boards (US) | Gaia Dynamics
results.content:
Bare (unpopulated) printed circuit boards are classified under HTS heading 8534, the dedicated provision for printed circuits. All bare PCBs are duty-free, with the 10-digit statistical breakouts distinguishing the board by the number of conductive layers, the substrate (impregnated paper, ceramic or other), and whether the board is the flexible type. An important distinction is that heading 8534 is for the bare board only; once components are mounted to create a printed circuit assembly, the [...] Bare printed circuit boards under heading 8534 enter the United States duty-free at a 0% general rate, across all the layer, substrate and flexible-type breakouts. Because the regular duty is free, the reason to identify the precise 10-digit code is accurate statistical reporting. Note that populated boards (printed circuit assemblies) are classified elsewhere as parts of the host device and may carry different duty treatment, and separate trade measures can apply to circuit boards and [...] | HTS Code | Description | Duty Rate |
 --- 
| 8534.00.00.20 | Printed circuits - with 3 or more layers of conducting materials  Bare multilayer PCB (3+ conductive layers) | Free |
| 8534.00.00.40 | Printed circuits - other (fewer than 3 conducting layers)  Bare single/double-sided PCB | Free |
| 8534.00.00.50 | Printed circuits - having a base wholly of impregnated paper  Bare PCB on paper-based (e.g., FR-1/FR-2) substrate | Free |

results.title: Tariffs on Electronics: What's Exempt and What's Not
results.content:
Even 2-4 layer rigid PCBs, which are temporarily exempt from Section 301, still face 145% total duties - a major challenge for cost-competitive, import-reliant designs.

### Classification Matters: HTS Codes for PCBs and PCBAs

Proper HTS classification is essential to managing tariff exposure.  PCBs and PCBAs often fall under:

 8534 - Printed Circuits (bare boards)
 8537 - Control panels or assemblies
 8542 - Electronic integrated circuits [...] These categories have been prioritized to support CHIPS Act goals and preserve domestic access to advanced computing and semiconductor components.

### PCB Tariffs and Exemptions: What's Still Fully Taxed?

Despite advocacy from industry groups, relief for PCBs and PCBAs remains limited.  The following products are still subject to the full 170% tariff burden when imported from China:

 6+ layer rigid PCBs
 All other bare PCB types
 Fully assembled PCBAs [...] The IPC (Institute for Printed Circuits) recently published a list of HTS codes that are exempt from the new 125% reciprocal tariff.  These exemptions offer targeted relief to strategic areas of the electronics supply chain, such as:

 Semiconductor devices (e.g., diodes, transistors, LEDs)
 Solid-stage storage (SSDs, memory cards)
 Data processing equipment (servers, CPUs, peripheral parts)
 Telecommunication devices (routers, wireless modules)
 Flat panel and display modules

results.title: A Complete Guide to PCB Board HS Code Classification | Coreties Blog
results.content:
Think of a product’s HS code not as a random set of numbers, but as a universal language that tells customs officials its story. For bare, unpopulated printed circuit boards, that story begins with Chapter 8534. This is the specific identifier that tells everyone, from a customs agent in Singapore to one in Germany, that you’re shipping a bare printed circuit. [...] The main HS code for a printed circuit board is 8534, which covers bare, unpopulated printed circuits. But that simple number is just the beginning. The correct code changes dramatically the moment you add components, turning that bare board into a Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA). Getting this distinction right is the single most important step to avoiding expensive shipping delays and customs fines.
